t.7.84.1: While that supreme and wondrous sacrifice was proceeding in this manner, Vālmīki, the foremost of sages, came swiftly, together with his disciples.
t.7.84.2: Having seen the sacrifice, godlike in splendour and wondrous to behold, he built beautiful huts in a secluded spot among the enclosures of the sages.
t.7.84.4: In the holy enclosures of the ṛṣis and in the dwellings of brāhmaṇas, on the streets and the royal highways, and in the houses of kings,
t.7.84.3: Delighted, he said to his two disciples: "You two, going forth with focused minds, sing the entire Rāmāyaṇa poem with the greatest joy."
t.7.84.5: At the door of Rāma's palace, and wherever the sacrificial rite is being performed, and especially in front of the officiating priests, there it should be sung.
t.7.84.6: And here are these fruits, sweet and of many kinds, grown on the mountain peaks; tasting them again and again, let the song be sung.
t.7.84.7: Dear sons, having eaten fruits and well-cleaned roots, you two will not grow weary, and you shall keep away from the city.
t.7.84.8: If Rāma, lord of the earth, should summon you to be heard, then the song is to be sung before the seated ṛṣis who are engaged in the proceedings.
t.7.84.9: Twenty cantos are to be sung each day with the greatest joy, in their many measures, just as I directed you before.
t.7.84.10: Nor should even the slightest greed be harboured out of a desire for wealth. What use is wealth to those who dwell in hermitages and live on fruits and roots?
t.7.84.11: If that Kākutstha should ask, "Whose boys are you two?", then you two should say thus to the lord of men: "We are indeed the disciples of Vālmīki."
t.7.84.12: Sounding these very sweet strings, or the register that was shown before, let the two of them sing most sweetly, free from all anxiety.
t.7.84.13: It should be sung from the very beginning, and not in disregard of the king; for by dharma the king is the father of all beings.
t.7.84.15: Having thus instructed them many times, the sage Vālmīki, son of Pracetas, supremely noble and of great renown, then fell silent.
t.7.84.14: You two, then, with joyful hearts, should tomorrow at daybreak sing that sweet song with full concentration, accompanied by the strings of the lute and in proper rhythm.
t.7.84.16: Having laid up in their hearts that wondrous and auspicious speech spoken by the sage, the two princes, full of eager longing, passed the night happily, like the two Aśvins refined by the counsel of Bhārgava.
